experiments.research_question: Can a dense model with at least one billion unique trainable parameters complete a finite forward, backward, and SGD update on the audited 8 GiB GPU in under ten minutes?
experiments.hypothesis: A 1,007,710,208-parameter BF16 Transformer with activation checkpointing and stateless SGD completes one update in <=540 seconds without exceeding available VRAM.
experiments.scientific_rationale: A minimal dense mechanism baseline is required before sparse or low-rank substitutes can be compared honestly.
experiments.independent_variable: One-billion dense model execution under BF16+SGD minimum-state configuration.
experiments.baseline: Analytic 6ND feasibility bound plus measured BF16 GEMM ceiling; no useful-quality baseline exists yet.
experiments.dataset: Deterministic synthetic byte corpus; mechanism test only
experiments.model: 20 layers, width 2048, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4, exactly 1,007,710,208 unique parameters
experiments.hardware_environment: ASUS G614JV; i7-13650HX; 15.63 GiB RAM; RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8,188 MiB
experiments.software_environment: Pinned uv/PyTorch environment recorded by the run
experiments.expected_result: One finite update may fit, but useful pretraining within ten minutes is rejected by the optimistic compute bound.
experiments.interpretation: The dense memory/finite-update mechanism gate passed. Eight synthetic bytes provide no useful-pretraining evidence.

experiments.research_question: Does direct BF16 SGD at learning rate 1e-4 measurably learn the repeated synthetic byte task over 256 steps?
experiments.hypothesis: Validation bits/byte decreases materially over 2,048 tokens.
experiments.scientific_rationale: The mechanism pass must be extended beyond one update to detect low-precision stagnation.
experiments.independent_variable: 256 direct-BF16 SGD steps at learning rate 1e-4.
experiments.model: 1,007,710,208-parameter dense BF16 Transformer
experiments.expected_result: Potential stagnation because clipped per-parameter updates fall below BF16 rounding quanta.
experiments.interpretation: Validation improved only 0.029%; the first-to-last training-loss window did not improve. Direct low-rate BF16 updates stagnated.

experiments.research_question: Can higher-learning-rate direct BF16 SGD learn the repeated byte task?
experiments.hypothesis: Learning rate 1e-2 overcomes enough rounding loss to reduce validation bits/byte.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Controls learning-rate scale before attributing gains to error feedback.
experiments.independent_variable: Direct BF16 SGD at learning rate 1e-2 for 128 steps.
experiments.model: 1,007,710,208-parameter dense BF16 Transformer
experiments.expected_result: Loss should decline, with potential instability from coarse updates.
experiments.interpretation: The high-rate direct control learned the trivial distribution, so EXP-1002 failure was not solely model size.

experiments.research_question: Does same-dtype residual error feedback improve 1B BF16 SGD time-to-quality?
experiments.hypothesis: ResidualSGD reduces time-to-EXP-1003 final quality by at least 2x without unacceptable memory or energy regression.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Kahan/error-feedback prior art can preserve updates rounded away by direct BF16 weight storage.
experiments.independent_variable: Optimizer: ResidualSGD versus direct SGD.
experiments.model: 1,007,710,208-parameter dense BF16 Transformer
experiments.expected_result: Better sample efficiency but extra parameter-sized memory and update time.
experiments.interpretation: Residual feedback improved sample efficiency and final quality but missed the 2x wall-time gate and nearly doubled energy while adding about 2 GiB state.

experiments.research_question: Can the dense 1B BF16 model reduce held-out loss on a repeated synthetic corpus and persist a checkpoint in under ten minutes?
experiments.hypothesis: 2,048 SGD steps plus a final checkpoint complete under 600 seconds and reduce validation bits/byte below 3.0.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Separates a persisted narrow memorization result from one-step mechanism and useful-pretraining claims.
experiments.independent_variable: Longer 2,048-step direct SGD run with final checkpoint persistence.
experiments.baseline: Initial random model and EXP-1003 short control
experiments.dataset: 100KB repeated synthetic byte training corpus; same-distribution validation prefix
experiments.model: 1,007,710,208-parameter dense BF16 Transformer
experiments.expected_result: Narrow corpus loss falls; result does not transfer to useful language pretraining.
experiments.interpretation: The narrow memorization and persistence gate passed in 4m17s. The corpus, context, and token count are far too small for a useful-pretraining claim.

experiments.research_question: Which sequence shape maximizes raw dense-1B training throughput while retaining at least 1 GiB estimated VRAM headroom?
experiments.hypothesis: Longer sequences will expose substantially more GPU parallelism than context 8 without exceeding the memory safety margin.
experiments.scientific_rationale: The prior mechanism run used a pathologically small shape and cannot represent the GPU's sustained token capacity.
experiments.independent_variable: Context length from 8 through 2048 at micro-batch one.
experiments.baseline: Context length 8 candidate in the same saturation runner.
experiments.dataset: Deterministic repeated synthetic byte corpus; throughput benchmark only
experiments.model: Dense Transformer near 1.01B parameters; position embedding size varies slightly with context
experiments.expected_result: Throughput rises with context until compute or attention cost saturates, while activation checkpointing holds memory below the gate.
experiments.interpretation: The original tiny sequence severely underutilized the GPU. Raw token throughput saturated near context 1024; this is not evidence of faster convergence.

experiments.research_question: Does the raw shape-saturation gain survive an equal-token quality comparison?
experiments.hypothesis: Context 128 processes 16,384 tokens faster and reaches the EXP-1005 validation target of 2.92159 bits/byte.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Raw tokens/second is valuable only if reduced optimizer-update count does not destroy time-to-quality.
experiments.independent_variable: Context 128 for 128 updates versus context 8 for 2048 updates, holding total training tokens at 16,384.
experiments.model: 1,007,955,968-parameter context-128 model versus 1,007,710,208-parameter baseline
experiments.expected_result: The candidate may be faster but lose sample efficiency because it performs sixteen times fewer optimizer updates.
experiments.interpretation: Shape saturation greatly improved raw throughput and energy at equal tokens but did not preserve quality because update count fell. It is not a learning-efficiency improvement.

experiments.research_question: Can MOLT train, checkpoint, reload, evaluate, and generate from a dense 1B GPT-style model using the supplied TinyStories file?
experiments.hypothesis: A 1B BF16 model completes 1,024 context-512 SGD updates under eight minutes, lowers held-out bits/byte, persists a verified checkpoint, and produces at least partially structured text.
experiments.scientific_rationale: An end-to-end real-text artifact is required to test the platform beyond repeated synthetic memorization.
experiments.independent_variable: Training a randomly initialized dense 1B byte Transformer on a deterministic TinyStories split.
experiments.baseline: Random initialization at step zero; no comparable trained 1B baseline is claimed.
experiments.dataset: D:/Projects/MOLT AI/Dataset/TinyStories-valid.txt; deterministic 17.5MB train and 1.9MB held-out splits
experiments.model: 20 layers, width 2048, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4, 1,008,742,400 unique parameters
experiments.hardware_environment: Audited RTX 4060 Laptop GPU and 16GB system RAM
experiments.expected_result: Loss should fall, while coherent generation is unlikely at only 524,288 training bytes.
experiments.interpretation: The full infrastructure gate passed and held-out statistics improved substantially. The generation-quality sub-hypothesis failed; the model is not useful at this training budget.
confounding_factors: thermal throttling up to an observed 90C
validation sample only 1,024 bytes per checkpoint

experiments.research_question: Can an approximately 50M-parameter industry-style subword Transformer train over the full supplied corpus for multiple epochs and generate readable stories on the audited consumer laptop?
experiments.hypothesis: A 49,883,520-parameter FP32-master/BF16-compute AdamW model completes two sequential BPE-token epochs under 15 minutes, reaches held-out perplexity below 50, and produces readable multi-sentence English.
experiments.scientific_rationale: The 1B byte model was too undertrained; a compute/data-matched model with proper tokenization is required to test useful local pretraining.
experiments.independent_variable: ByteLevel BPE plus a compute-matched 49.88M decoder trained for two full corpus passes.
experiments.baseline: Random initialization at step zero; MOLT AI 1B byte v1 as a qualitative failed-tokenization reference only.
experiments.dataset: 4,413,694 training and 231,510 held-out ByteLevel BPE tokens from the supplied TinyStories file
experiments.model: 9 layers, width 640, 10 heads, 49,883,520 unique parameters, 8,192-token tied vocabulary
experiments.hardware_environment: Audited RTX 4060 Laptop GPU and 16GB system RAM
experiments.expected_result: The smaller subword model should use the available data/compute far more effectively than the 1B byte model.
experiments.interpretation: All registered single-run infrastructure and quality gates passed. Story semantics and grammar remain imperfect, and no multi-seed generalization claim is made.
confounding_factors: subjective readable-output gate backed by raw samples

experiments.research_question: Can answer-masked supervised adaptation add correct Roxy question answering without misrepresenting general conversational ability?
experiments.hypothesis: Answer-only loss produces the expected big-leaves answer for direct and held-out paraphrase prompts while held-out answer loss improves.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Instruction tuning should optimize assistant tokens rather than spend equal loss on prompt reproduction.
experiments.independent_variable: Unmasked QA causal loss versus answer-only target masking, with 20-step and 200-step masked checkpoints.
experiments.baseline: Unmasked QA v1 and clean EXP-1012 base checkpoint.
experiments.dataset: 991-token reviewed QA train split and 106-token held-out paraphrase split; 492/48 supervised answer tokens
experiments.model: EXP-1012 architecture initialized from its validated checkpoint
experiments.expected_result: Masking should improve factual answer behavior; the tiny dataset may overfit rapidly.
success_thresholds: held-out paraphrase answer contains big leaves
experiments.interpretation: Answer masking fixed the prompt-repetition failure. The behavioral specialist requires overfitting relative to aggregate held-out loss, so it is narrow and not a general instruction model.

experiments.research_question: Can BL-0001 produce reproducible quality, performance, memory, energy, and recovery measurements on the audited host?
experiments.hypothesis: The specified 6,449,664-parameter baseline will complete three exact 50M-token runs below 12 GiB process RAM and 7.0 GiB steady VRAM with trustworthy telemetry and resume behavior.
experiments.scientific_rationale: A stable, small from-scratch workload is required before an efficiency method can be compared without instrumentation or operational confounds.
experiments.independent_variable: Random seed across full runs; fixed seed across short system-noise repetitions.
experiments.dataset: roneneldan/TinyStories pinned revision; source-order 20,000,000-byte train prefix and 2,000,000-byte validation prefix
experiments.model: 8-layer byte Transformer, width 256, 8 heads, MLP 1024, expected 6,449,664 parameters
experiments.hardware_environment: ASUS G614JV; i7-13650HX; 15.63 GiB RAM; RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8,188 MiB; Windows 11 build 26200
experiments.software_environment: Not yet created; must be resolved from uv lockfile and recorded per run
experiments.expected_result: All baseline acceptance gates pass; this is a hypothesis, not an observed result.
failure_thresholds: any full seed misses exact token budget

experiments.research_question: Can loss-slope-triggered progressive freezing save backward time and energy without material quality loss?
experiments.hypothesis: A plateau-triggered layer-freezing policy saves at least 20% GPU energy-to-quality with <=1% final validation bits/byte regression in a full test.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Prior progressive-freezing results are architecture-dependent; an explicit signal may avoid premature fixed-schedule freezing.
experiments.independent_variable: Freezing policy: none, fixed schedule, or pre-registered plateau trigger.
experiments.baseline: BL-0001 AdamW with no freezing; reduced-shape equivalent for cheap falsification
experiments.model: Cheap test: 2 layers, width 128; full test only after survival: BL-0001
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; published evidence includes both gains and failures across architectures.
success_thresholds: cheap test saves >=10% training-phase time in both seeds
failure_thresholds: either cheap seed exceeds 2% quality regression
confounding_factors: gradient norm is not causal importance

experiments.research_question: Does GaLore-style low-rank gradient projection reduce end-to-end peak VRAM on this small Windows workload without unacceptable regression?
experiments.hypothesis: Projection reduces peak VRAM by at least 30% with <=20% time-to-target and <=1% final quality regression in a full test.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Reported optimizer-state savings may be offset by projection overhead or full-gradient peaks at local scale.
experiments.independent_variable: AdamW versus GaLore-style projection rank and refresh cadence.
experiments.baseline: BL-0001 AdamW; transparent deterministic optimizer reference for correctness
experiments.dataset: Synthetic correctness fixture, then BL-0001 byte slice
experiments.model: Linear reference and 2-layer reduced model; BL-0001 only after survival
experiments.software_environment: Pinned Milestone 1 environment plus reviewed implementation pin if reused
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; overhead may dominate at 6.45M parameters.

experiments.research_question: Can deduplication and cheap diversity-aware pruning reduce end-to-end tokens/time-to-quality after preparation cost?
experiments.hypothesis: Deduplication plus constrained reference scoring reduces tokens-to-target by at least 20% with <=1% held-out quality regression in a full test.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Published data-selection gains may not amortize scoring cost or transfer to the synthetic TinyStories distribution.
experiments.independent_variable: Raw, deduplicated, random-pruned, or diversity/score-pruned data stream.
experiments.baseline: BL-0001 unfiltered stream; random-pruned control in full test
experiments.model: 2-layer reduced model for cheap falsification; BL-0001 after survival
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; synthetic repetition may help or make pruning distributionally harmful.

experiments.research_question: Does explicitly retaining the Transformer residual stream in BF16 reduce peak VRAM while FP32 parameters and AdamW states are preserved?
experiments.hypothesis: Explicit BF16 residual activations reduce peak allocated VRAM by at least 30% with <=10% throughput regression.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Embedding outputs can remain FP32 under autocast, potentially promoting residual additions and retaining wider saved tensors.
experiments.independent_variable: model.activation_dtype parameter versus bfloat16
experiments.baseline: 50M BPE pretraining saturation result at context 512 and microbatch 24
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT AI decoder
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB and audited Windows host
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; allocator and autocast behavior may make the explicit cast redundant.
experiments.result: Peak allocation 4,748,241,408 bytes versus approximately 4,747,487,744 baseline; throughput 48,186 versus 47,538 tokens/s.
experiments.interpretation: The expected memory saving did not occur; the throughput difference is not enough to establish a gain without repeats.

experiments.research_question: Can full block activation recomputation halve allocated VRAM at equal quality without a major time or energy regression?
experiments.hypothesis: Recomputation cuts allocated VRAM by >=50% with <=10% time and <=1% final-quality regression.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Discarding block intermediates and recomputing them during backward trades arithmetic for activation storage.
experiments.independent_variable: activation_checkpointing false versus true
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT AI decoder
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB and audited Windows host
experiments.expected_result: Lower memory with a measurable recomputation penalty; whether it crosses the gate was unknown.
experiments.result: Perplexity 33.7086 versus 33.7011; allocated VRAM 2,372,921,856 versus 4,745,062,912 bytes (-49.992%); time 272.423 versus 225.257 seconds (+20.94%); energy 18,666.36 versus 16,543.64 joules (+12.83%).
experiments.interpretation: Mechanism is useful for constrained fit and gives essentially half allocation, but fails the strict memory threshold by 0.008 percentage points and exceeds the time regression limit.

experiments.research_question: Can sequence-length warmup reach the fixed context-512 target quality in half the time or energy?
experiments.hypothesis: A preregistered 128-to-256-to-512 schedule reaches 5.075 bits/token using <=60% of baseline time and board energy in the first full test.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Early optimization may not require full-length attention; shorter sequences reduce quadratic attention work and can support more efficient batches.
experiments.independent_variable: fixed context 512 versus preregistered context schedule
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT AI decoder with context capacity 512
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB and audited Windows host
experiments.expected_result: Unknown locally; prior work reports large gains at GPT-2 scales.
failure_thresholds: neither development schedule improves time-to-target by 25%

experiments.research_question: Can coupled suffix losses and randomized context corrections provide an unbiased full-context Transformer gradient at more than twice the variance-adjusted progress per second?
experiments.hypothesis: Nested contexts 64, 128, and 512 with sampled importance-weighted corrections achieve >=2x raw speed and >=1x variance-adjusted speed without increasing peak allocation; a survivor would advance to multi-seed training.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Short causal contexts are cheaper, while a telescoping identity can preserve the exact longest-context objective in expectation if adjacent gradient corrections have sufficiently small variance.
experiments.independent_variable: Exact context-512 suffix gradient versus randomized coupled-suffix telescoping gradient and its correction probabilities.
experiments.baseline: Exact context-512 gradient on the identical final 64 targets.
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT AI decoder with context capacity 512.
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB and audited Windows host.
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; correction gradient variance may dominate the compute saving.
success_thresholds: candidate adjusted peak allocation <= exact reference
experiments.result: Exact unbiasedness tests passed. At batch 8 and p=(0.1,0.1), measured raw speed was 3.152x but gradient second moment was 12.123x, giving a 0.260x proxy. Exact grid search selected p=(1,1), identical to the full-context baseline, at 1.0x. Candidate proxy peak allocation also exceeded reference.
experiments.interpretation: Adjacent context gradients were too different for rare unbiased corrections. Generic randomized telescoping is established prior art, so no novelty claim survives. Full optimizer and multi-seed runs were correctly skipped by the preregistered kill rule.
confounding_factors: variance-adjusted score is a proxy rather than convergence

experiments.research_question: Which semantically invariant execution settings form the time/energy-to-target frontier for the immutable 49.88M workload?
experiments.hypothesis: At least one execution configuration improves both target-time and target-energy by 1% without more than 1% final-NLL regression.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Utilization and precision can alter board power and throughput without changing the intended optimizer workload.
experiments.independent_variable: Microbatch/accumulation, packing implementation, precision, optimizer fusion, SDPA dispatch, compile support and safe power mode.
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT decoder, context 512
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB; firmware power ceiling varied and manual limit was unsupported
experiments.software_environment: Pinned MOLT environment; PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 on Windows
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; a joint optimum was plausible but thermal state was a known confounder.
success_thresholds: >=1% repeatable improvement in target-time and target-energy
measurements: seconds and NVML board joules to interpolated target NLL
experiments.result: Microbatch 24/accumulation 1 was the static execution winner. Low-power BF16 saved 30.57% energy but was 33.12% slower. FP16 was slower than low-power BF16 for only 0.40% energy reduction.
experiments.interpretation: No joint winner was demonstrated. Firmware state, not MOLT, explains the large frontier separation.

experiments.research_question: Can a live loss-conditioned time-energy controller beat the strongest static execution configuration?
experiments.hypothesis: Conservative action switching improves both time and energy by >=1% after including exploration cost.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Loss progress could prevent a systems-efficient but optimization-inefficient configuration from being selected, while enforced-power telemetry could expose state-dependent execution optima.
experiments.independent_variable: Static microbatch 24 versus controller exploration of microbatch 24 and 12 at fixed effective batch 24.
experiments.model: 49,883,520-parameter MOLT decoder, context 512
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB, enforced ceiling 115W during kill test
experiments.software_environment: Pinned MOLT environment; PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 on Windows
experiments.expected_result: Likely rejection because the static sweep already showed one action dominating.
success_thresholds: >=1% improvement in both measured time and board energy
failure_thresholds: controller merely returns to static winner
experiments.result: Controller was 1.592% slower and used 3.054% more board energy; it explored microbatch 12 for two blocks and returned to 24.
experiments.interpretation: Exploration overhead cannot amortize in this one-shot workload because the tested alternative is dominated. Training loss is also too noisy for short-horizon projection.

experiments.research_question: Does packed-NF4 H2D prefetch on a second CUDA stream improve time and energy over synchronous streamed LoRA layers?
experiments.hypothesis: At identical residual-linear work, double buffering improves both time and GPU board energy by at least 1% without changing outputs or gradients.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Copying the next packed layer during current-layer matrix multiplication could hide PCIe latency if transfer is a material critical-path component.
experiments.independent_variable: Synchronous packed transfer versus two-slot asynchronous packed transfer; dequantization remains on the compute stream.
experiments.dataset: Synthetic activation tensor; mechanism test only
experiments.model: Eight frozen NF4 residual linear layers with GPU-resident LoRA
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; small packed transfers may be too cheap to amortize stream synchronization and allocator overhead.
experiments.result: Double buffering reached 5,697.15 activation vectors/s versus 5,933.73 synchronously, a 3.99% throughput regression; sampled board energy was also higher.
experiments.interpretation: Packed transfer was not the dominant critical path at this shape. Stream management and overlap offered no recoverable benefit.
confounding_factors: synthetic residual-linear rather than decoder workload

experiments.research_question: Does grouping four NF4 streamed layers per copy/compute dependency produce at least 10% end-to-end speedup over synchronous transfer?
experiments.hypothesis: K=4 amortizes stream waits enough to improve full forward/backward/update throughput by at least 10% without energy, memory, or thermal regression.
experiments.scientific_rationale: One dependency can cover four packed transfers while the other bundle computes, reducing eight waits to two for an eight-layer fixture.
experiments.independent_variable: Synchronous transfer versus grouped K=4 copy-stream transfer.
experiments.dataset: Synthetic activation tensor; mechanism test only
experiments.model: Eight frozen NF4 residual linear layers with GPU-resident LoRA
experiments.expected_result: Fewer stream dependencies may help only if host transfer and dispatch are on the critical path.
experiments.result: Paired throughput changes were -11.77%, +4.11%, and +4.11%; median +4.11%. Board energy was mixed. An earlier 30-step +10.50% result did not reproduce.
experiments.interpretation: Wait amortization is real (eight waits become two), but it is not the dominant cost and did not produce the required repeatable gain.
confounding_factors: fixed execution order within each pair

experiments.research_question: Can the requested Windows fusion and context-512/batch-24 profile pass the 40% memory, 35k tokens/s, and 70 C gates on this host?
experiments.hypothesis: Max-autotune fusion reduces incremental activation/backward allocation by >=40%, while the production profile sustains >=35k tokens/s at <=70 C.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Kernel fusion can remove intermediates and the selected geometry can raise GPU occupancy.
experiments.independent_variable: Eager versus max-autotune compiled forward; production benchmark geometry.
experiments.model: 10,776,640-parameter MOLT SLM throughput fixture
experiments.software_environment: PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128; optional triton-windows 3.4.0.post21; no MSVC, nvcc, Ninja, CUDA_HOME or Liger
experiments.expected_result: Throughput likely passes for the small fixture; fusion depends on missing toolchain; thermal state is uncertain.
experiments.result: No-graph max-autotune fusion worked and reduced incremental allocation 14.37%, below the 40% gate; graph-enabled max-autotune failed in the Windows static launcher. Eager brief throughput was 127,854 tokens/s at 71 C; compiled briefly reached 175,256 tokens/s but hit 74 C after warm-up.
experiments.interpretation: Only short-window small-model throughput and partial no-graph fusion survived. Graph capture, 40% memory reduction, thermal reliability, large-model memory, and commercial readiness did not.
confounding_factors: very short interval before thermal abort

experiments.research_question: Does Windows max-autotune fusion without CUDA Graphs improve both end-to-end time and GPU-board energy to target quality without memory, thermal, reliability or quality regression?
experiments.hypothesis: On static context-512 geometry, compiled fusion improves median time-to-target and board-energy-to-target by at least 1% while final validation NLL remains within 1% of eager and peak allocation does not regress.
experiments.scientific_rationale: The local mechanism probe showed faster cached forward/backward and 14.37% less incremental allocation, but excluded optimizer, convergence, compilation amortization and reliable thermal control.
experiments.independent_variable: Eager PyTorch versus compile-max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
experiments.baseline: Strongest eager context-512 batch-24 contiguous profile
experiments.dataset: Prepared TinyStories BPE-8192 training and validation streams
experiments.model: 10,776,640-parameter kill fixture, followed only on survival by immutable 49,883,520-parameter workload
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB, paired starting-temperature bins on AC power
experiments.expected_result: Unknown; compiler speed may be offset by compilation cost, thermal load or convergence differences.
measurements: NVML board joules to interpolated target NLL
experiments.result: Not run. Preregistered before implementing the paired runner.
experiments.interpretation: No conclusion and no novelty claim.
confounding_factors: NVML excludes CPU and wall-plug energy
laptop cooling is not directly controllable
Windows Triton fork rather than upstream-supported Windows backend

experiments.research_question: Can bounded 30-50 ms inter-step duty cycling hold the RTX 4060 Laptop GPU at <=62 C while sustaining >=150k tokens/s for the requested batch-16/accumulation-2 workload?
experiments.hypothesis: Pausing only above 60 C removes enough heat to complete all steps without crossing 72 C while retaining >=150k measured tokens/s.
experiments.scientific_rationale: Short idle gaps allow fan cooling, but the achievable equilibrium depends on actual power control and laptop cooling capacity.
experiments.independent_variable: Temperature-triggered bounded micro-pauses under the cool profile.
experiments.dataset: D:/Projects/MOLT AI/custom/data/prepared train and validation int32 tokens
experiments.model: 10,776,640-parameter MOLT SLM
experiments.hardware_environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8GB; requested 65 W rejected; actual enforced limit 115 W
experiments.expected_result: Likely rejection if firmware power cannot be reduced because earlier compiled probes reached 74 C.
experiments.result: 65 W set failed with insufficient permissions; enforced limit stayed 115 W. Five warm-up plus 8 measured steps reached 74 C and aborted. Twelve pauses totaled 0.4933 s. Throughput was 115,172.5 tokens/s.
experiments.interpretation: The controller works as implemented but the specified pause ceiling cannot satisfy both cooling and throughput on this power/cooling state.
